@@ -4,6 +4,12 @@ These tests exercise a bundled provider process against a synthetic local model

These are distinct from `../e2e/`, whose prioritized cross-provider suites replay model traffic captured from real CAPI interactions and assert AHP snapshots and real tool behavior. Provider integration tests do not contribute to the E2E coverage report.

+`copilotGrepSearchNudge.integrationTest.ts` exercises the default-off `chat.copilot.searchSubagent.grepNudge` experiment with the bundled Copilot runtime and a synthetic model. During the first two real user messages, a primary-agent `grep` or `rg` call is deferred only if the runtime currently offers `search_code_subagent`. The model receives a suggestion and the live tool schema; it can make an ordinary search-subagent call or repeat identical grep arguments. One identical retry consumes the pending nudge and continues through existing plugin hooks and permissions, without granting approval. Further calls can be nudged again. Child-agent searches are unaffected. The flag is checked before any history or tool-metadata RPC. When enabled, the first eligible grep initializes a bounded history snapshot once, including for resumed conversations; concurrent calls share that initialization. Existing user-message events update a set of at most three IDs, deduplicating live echoes against history. Once three real user messages are known, subsequent grep calls perform neither RPC. Pending retries are scoped to the current user message and are not persisted across host restarts. Advisory lookup failures are logged and leave ordinary tool checks intact; failed history initialization can be retried. The experiment trigger covers primary grep attempts in both arms, a broader population than confirmed nudge eligibility, so the control arm needs no eligibility RPCs. The tests verify that hook-time SDK queries do not deadlock, that the model receives the nudge, that a retry returns actual file contents, and that an alternative search-subagent call completes successfully.

Every real provider process must use a temporary home through `createIsolatedProviderEnvironment` or the required `homeDir` option of `startRealServer`. This keeps provider configuration, logs, and sessions out of the developer's real home directory.

`copilotCredentialSponsorship.integrationTest.ts` drives the real `CopilotAgent` and bundled SDK using the production service registrations and launcher. A protected client-factory override supplies isolated homes and loopback GitHub/CAPI endpoints without sanitizing the product's environment. The fixture clears real credential inputs and seeds fake `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `COPILOT_SDK_AUTH_TOKEN`, and `OPENAI_API_KEY` sentinels before product startup. Credential-owned startup options, actual HTTP headers, and native shell-tool environments must exclude those sentinels; legacy L uses an explicit host-supplied credential. The server checks exact A/B/legacy-L model and Connector credentials, including idle rotation and startup-configuration replacement. Native `view`, `apply_patch`, `glob`, `rg`, and platform shell tools must execute successfully against synthetic files, not just appear in the model request. A/B shell commands verify the exact caller token by comparison without printing its value. The test also verifies repository instructions, workspace-discovered skills, environment context, and concurrent local deletion after idle release without HTTP traffic or a sponsor. Canonical OS-temporary directories must be outside the source workspace, use nested Git roots, and must not inherit this repository's instructions. This is provider-boundary coverage, not AHP conformance, network containment, or real-service authentication qualification.
